exemplar.title: What strong work looks like
exemplar.intro: A strong package pitch proves both volume and surface area — here is how one student designed a juice box.

traits.sample: My juice box is 4 cm × 6 cm × 10 cm, so V = 4 × 6 × 10 = 240 cubic centimeters — enough for 240 mL of juice.
traits.why: Every dimension is named and the units are cubic.

traits.trait: Finds surface area from the net
traits.sample: I drew a connected six-face net, labeled the three face pairs, and calculated 2(24) + 2(40) + 2(60) = 248 cm².
traits.why: The student-drawn, labeled net is direct 6.GR.4 evidence and shows no face was missed.

traits.sample: My tall design holds the same 240 cm³ but uses 12 cm² less material than the cube version, so it is cheaper to make.
traits.why: Volume-to-surface-area comparison is the heart of package design.

traits.trait: Turns math into a cost argument
traits.sample: At the illustrative rate of $0.02 per cm², one box uses $4.96 of raw cardboard; that excludes cutting, printing, labor, and waste.
traits.why: The multiplication is correct and the scope of the illustrative cost is explicit.
